findings.title: chemtrails draws nearly the whole FUTURE trajectory as a 'past' trail for the first tail_duration seconds, then blinks empty (negative-slice bug)
findings.description: update_lines_parallel (matplotlib_backend.py:992-993) computes the chemtrail as data[0 : num - tail_duration + 1] where tail_duration is the window size in FRAMES. For every frame num < window-1 the stop index is NEGATIVE, so Python's negative indexing keeps the FIRST n_frames-(window-1-num) points: at frame 0 of a 48-frame animation with a 12-frame window the 'past trail' contains 37 of 48 points -- almost the entire trajectory, including the future -- and it GROWS to 47 points at frame 10, then blinks to 0 at frame 11 and regrows correctly from frame 12. With all-default parameters (duration=30, frame_rate=30, tail_duration=2 -> 900 frames, 60-frame window) the same bug paints ~93-99% of the trajectory as a faint trail for the first 2 seconds of EVERY chemtrails animation, then it visibly flickers off. The same expression exists in the 2-D path (update_lines_parallel_2d, matplotlib_backend.py:1697-1698). Two adjacent manifestations of the same slicing: (a) when the window covers the whole animation (default tail_duration with short durations) the trail exactly mirrors the head all animation long and then blinks EMPTY on the final frame (chemtrails.gif f23: trail 0 pts); (b) a dataset with fewer interpolated points than the window never shows any chemtrail at all ([40pt,15pt] test: trail stayed 0 pts for the short dataset through the last frame). Expected trail is max(0, num - window + 1) leading points -- i.e. data[0 : max(0, num - tail_duration + 1)].
findings.repro:

import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
t = np.linspace(0, 4*np.pi, 40)
d = np.column_stack([np.cos(t), np.sin(t), np.linspace(0,1,40)])
r = hyp.plot([d], animate=True, chemtrails=True, duration=4, tail_duration=1, frame_rate=12, show=False)
fig, ani = r
ax = fig.axes[0]
for num in [0, 5, 10, 11, 12]:
    ani._draw_frame(num)
    trail = [l for l in ax.lines if l.get_alpha() == 0.3][0]
    print(num, len(trail.get_data_3d()[0]))
"
findings.expected: Trail point counts 0,0,0,0,1 for frames 0,5,10,11,12 (nothing has left the 12-frame head window before frame 11).
findings.actual:

findings.title: animate + continuous/matrix hue silently renders static content on matplotlib: no reveal, no chemtrails/precog/bullettime; 2-D case saves a 1-frame GIF; plotly disagrees
findings.description: For continuous (or matrix) per-observation hue, plot.py builds the animated head/trail Line3D artists and the FuncAnimation first, then at plot.py:2673-2679 calls _apply_multicolor_lines, which 'swap[s] the single-color artists for per-segment-colored line collections' -- i.e. removes the very artists the frame callbacks update and replaces them with STATIC full-trajectory collections. Result: every frame of a parallel/chemtrails/precog/bullettime/window animation shows the ENTIRE multicolored trajectory at full opacity. In 3-D only the camera still rotates; in 2-D (no camera) all frames are pixel-identical, and the exported GIF collapses to a SINGLE frame. The QC 2026-07 fix (commit 23a: 'animate + per-observation hue no longer crashes') removed the crash but left the animation semantics broken, with no warning to the user. The plotly backend animates the identical call correctly (embedded frame point counts grow 2 -> 7 -> 21), so the two backends disagree. Categorical/group hue is unaffected (w2 group-hue bullettime renders perfectly).
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
from PIL import Image
t = np.linspace(0, 4*np.pi, 40)
d = np.column_stack([np.cos(t), np.sin(t), np.linspace(0,1,40)])
hyp.plot(d, ndims=2, animate=True, hue=np.linspace(0,1,40), duration=2, frame_rate=12, show=False, save_path='/tmp/hue2d.gif')
print('gif frames:', Image.open('/tmp/hue2d.gif').n_frames)
"
findings.expected: A 24-frame gif in which the multicolored 2-D trajectory is progressively revealed (like the no-hue control, which produces 24 distinct frames).
findings.actual: gif frames: 1  -- all 24 rendered frames are pixel-identical so Pillow merges them; the 'animation' is a static image. 3-D precog+hue evidence: s7_chue_precog_f04.png shows the full trajectory opaque at frame 4 vs s7_nohue_precog_f04.png showing the correct opaque-head + faint-future rendering. Plotly control: frame point counts [2,1]/[7,1]/[21,1] at frames 0/6/20.
docs_impact: hypertools/plot/plot.py (hue docstring says nothing about animation; either fix the behavior or document/warn)

findings.title: A 1-point dataset alongside a trajectory crashes plot() with a raw scipy error ([multi,single]) or silently yields a 1-frame animation ([single,multi])
findings.description: The line-interpolation gate in plot.py:2327 checks ONLY the first dataset: `if xform[0].shape[0] > 1: xform = interp_array_list(xform, ...)`. If any LATER dataset has a single row, interp_array calls scipy pchip on it and crashes with 'ValueError: `x` must contain at least 2 elements.' (affects STATIC plots too, same call). If the single-point dataset comes FIRST, NO dataset is interpolated and an animated plot gets frames = x[0].shape[0] = 1 -- a one-frame 'animation' with unsmoothed lines and no error. matplotlib_backend.py:1265-1269 explicitly documents that mixed fmts including single-point datasets (line fmt converted to '.') are supposed to work for animations, so the intended feature is unreachable through the default-fmt path. Workaround (verified): pass an explicit per-dataset fmt list, e.g. fmt=['-','.']. A trajectory plus a single reference/landmark point is a plausible scientific input.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
t = np.linspace(0, 4*np.pi, 40)
d = np.column_stack([np.cos(t), np.sin(t), np.linspace(0,1,40)])
pt = d[:1]
try:
    hyp.plot([d, pt], animate=True, duration=2, frame_rate=12, show=False)
except Exception as e:
    print('crash:', e)
r = hyp.plot([pt, d], animate=True, duration=2, frame_rate=12, show=False)
print('frames when single point first:', r.animation._save_count)
"

findings.title: animate='spin'/'parallel'/True/'window' ignore the azim= kwarg (camera always starts at azimuth 0); 'serial'/'morph' honor it
findings.description: update_lines_spin (matplotlib_backend.py:1040) computes azim_now = rotations * 360 * num/(frame_rate*duration) and update_lines_parallel (line 966) rotations * 360 * num/n_frames -- neither adds the user-supplied (or default -60) azim, so these styles always start the camera at azimuth 0. update_lines_serial (line 1080) and update_morph use azim + offset and honor it. Consequences: hyp.plot(..., animate='spin', azim=45) silently starts at 0; the first animation frame never matches the static view of the same data (static uses azim=-60); rotations=0 (a legitimate way to get a fixed-camera animation) cannot be combined with a chosen viewing angle.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
d = np.random.RandomState(0).randn(30, 3)
r = hyp.plot(d, animate='spin', azim=45, duration=1, frame_rate=6, show=False)
r.animation._draw_frame(0)
print('frame-0 azim:', r.figure.axes[0].azim)
"
findings.expected: frame-0 azim: 45.0 (as passed), matching how 'serial'/'morph' treat azim.
docs_impact: hypertools/plot/plot.py (azim docstring does not mention it is ignored for spin/parallel/window)

findings.title: Non-bool/non-string truthy animate values (e.g. animate=2) silently produce a STATIC plot
findings.description: plot.py's style whitelist (line 1322) only validates STRINGS: `if isinstance(animate, str) and animate not in (...)`. A truthy non-string like animate=2 (a user might mean '2 rotations' or truthiness) passes validation, triggers the animation code paths in plot() (backend switching etc.), but matplotlib_backend.py:1994 gates dispatch on `animate in [True, 'parallel', 'spin', 'serial', 'morph', 'window']` -- and 2 != True -- so it dispatches a STATIC plot. No error, no warning; plot() returns a plain Figure. Note the quirk that animate=1 WOULD animate (1 == True in Python) while animate=2 does not. animate=np.True_ works correctly (np.True_ == True).
findings.repro:

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:

    r = hyp.plot(d, animate=2, duration=1, frame_rate=6, show=False)
print(type(r).__name__, [str(x.message) for x in w])
"

findings.title: Trail flags as np.ndarray crash with a cryptic numpy message; str/dict values are silently coerced to True
findings.description: broadcast_trail_flag (trails.py:41-49) accepts only list/tuple for the per-dataset form; anything else goes through bool(value). chemtrails=np.array([True, False]) -- the natural result of any array computation -- raises 'ValueError: The truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous. Use a.any() or a.all()' without naming the chemtrails kwarg or the fix (pass a list). Meanwhile chemtrails='yes' or chemtrails={'0': True} silently become True-for-all-datasets. Suggest accepting ndarray alongside list/tuple (np.asarray(...).tolist()) and raising a named TypeError for other non-bool scalars.

findings.title: precog leaves a one-segment gap between the opaque head and the faint future trail
findings.description: In update_lines_parallel the head line ends at point index num (window slice data[num-w : num+1]) while the precog trail starts at index num+1 (data[num+1:]), so the segment connecting points num and num+1 is never drawn by either artist -- a visible break right at the head of the trajectory, most noticeable with few points/low frame rates. chemtrails does not have this problem (its trail slice data[0:num-w+1] ends at the head window's first point, sharing it). Fix: start the precog trail at data[num:].
findings.repro:

findings.title: duration=/frame_rate= are not honored for marker-only parallel animations (frame count = raw row count)
findings.description: For animate=True/'parallel' the frame count is x[0].shape[0] (matplotlib_backend.py:1608). Line fmts are interpolated to ~frame_rate*duration points so this works out (verified 24 frames for duration=2, frame_rate=12), but marker-only fmts ('.') skip interpolation entirely, so a 40-point dataset yields a 40-frame animation regardless of duration -- the exported gif plays 40/12 = 3.33 s instead of the requested 2 s. This contradicts the docstring's frame_rate claim 'Both backends generate exactly frame_rate * duration frames' (plot.py:862-866) and animate.py's comment 'its save_count (== frame_rate * duration) frames' (animate.py:22-27). spin/serial use int(round(frame_rate*duration)) and are unaffected (verified 12/24 frames for 1/2 s).

findings.title: Rows that are entirely NaN crash line plots (animated and static) with a raw scipy error instead of a hypertools message
findings.description: format_data's PPCA fill (ppca=True default) cannot reconstruct rows where EVERY feature is NaN, and plot.py only applies np.nan_to_num AFTER the interpolation step (nan_to_num at plot.py:2518 vs interp at 2323), so pchip receives NaNs and raises 'ValueError: `y` must contain only finite values.' -- a bare scipy traceback that names neither NaN nor the impute= escape hatch. Verified: full-row NaN crashes both animate='bullettime' and the STATIC plot of the same data (so the defect is plot-wide, reported here because animation workflows hit it); partial-row NaN works fine (PPCA fills it). Fully-missing samples are routine in neuro/behavioral timeseries.

findings.actual: ValueError: `y` must contain only finite values.  (raised from hypertools/_shared/helpers.py:140 interp_array -> scipy pchip; identical for the static plot)

findings.title: save_path with an unrecognized extension leaks a raw ffmpeg CalledProcessError instead of naming supported formats
findings.description: _save_animation (animate.py:44-47) routes any extension that is not svg/gif/png/apng to the ffmpeg writer, so save_path='anim.xyz' fails with subprocess.CalledProcessError dumping the entire ffmpeg command line ('Command '['ffmpeg', '-f', 'rawvideo', ...]' returned non-zero exit status 1'). A user typo (.gfi, .png3, .webm...) gets no hint that only gif/png/apng/svg/mp4/mov/avi are supported.
